ap_calculus_ab-m27-r1.explanation_en: The average value is (1/(9-0))∫0^9 (0.30+0.12√t)dt. The integral equals 0.30(9)+0.12(2/3)(27)=2.70+2.16=4.86, so the average is 4.86/9=0.54 dollars per hour. The option 4.86 is the total cost, because it is not divided by the interval length. The option 0.48 averages the endpoint values 0.30 and 0.66, which ignores the curvature of the square-root model. The option 0.49 divides the integral by 10 instead of by the length of the interval, which is 9.

ap_calculus_ab-m28-r0.stem: A field team models two sediment layer boundaries in a stream bank cross-section by $f(x)=x$ and $g(x)=x^2-2x+2$, where $x$ is distance from the bank in meters and the graphs are shown. Which expression gives the total area of the region between the two curves for $0\le x\le 3$?
ap_calculus_ab-m28-r0.stimulus: {"kind":"graph","description":"Two curves on [0,3]: a straight line f and a parabola g that cross at x=1 and x=2.","data":{"x_axis":{"label":"distance from bank x (m)","min":0,"max":3},"y_axis":{"label":"depth below marker (m)","min":0,"max":5},"curves":[{"label":"f","expression":"x","points":[[0,0],[1,1],[2,2],[3,3]]},{"label":"g","expression":"x^2 - 2x + 2","points":[[0,2],[1,1],[2,2],[3,5]]}],"intersections":[[1,1],[2,2]],"sign_note":"g(x) > f(x) on (0,1); f(x) > g(x) on (1,2); g(x) > f(x) on (2,3)","region":"between the curves for 0<=x<=3"}

options.why: Correct: splits at both crossings x=1 and x=2 and uses upper minus lower on each piece (g-f, then f-g, then g-f).
Uses g-f over the whole interval, ignoring that the curves cross; positive and negative parts partly cancel, so this is a signed value, not area.
Reverses upper and lower on every piece, so each integrand has the wrong sign (the total is the negative of the area).
Splits only at x=2 and misses the crossing at x=1, so the integrand sign is wrong on part of the first piece.

ap_calculus_ab-m28-r0.explanation_en: Setting x = x^2 - 2x + 2 gives x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0, so the curves cross at x=1 and x=2, both inside [0,3]. Area between curves is the integral of (upper minus lower), so the interval must be split at each crossing. On (0,1) g is above f, so the integrand is g-f = x^2-3x+2; on (1,2) f is above g, so the integrand is f-g = -x^2+3x-2; on (2,3) g is above f again. The three-piece sum with these integrands is the area (it equals 1/6 + 1/6 + 5/6 = 7/6). A single integral of g-f over [0,3] is a signed quantity: the negative middle piece partly cancels the positive outer pieces, so it is not the area. The option that reverses upper and lower on every piece has the wrong sign everywhere and gives the negative of the area. The option that splits only at x=2 treats g-f as the integrand on all of [0,2], but f is above g on (1,2), so the first piece is a signed value that cancels part of its area.

ap_calculus_ab-m28-r1.stem: A shop owner compares the projected profit rates of two product lines over the first 3 months. Line P has profit rate $f(x)=x^2-2x+3$ and Line Q has profit rate $g(x)=x+1$, both in thousands of dollars per month, as shown in the graph. The owner wants the total size of the gap between the two profit rates, counting every month's gap as positive no matter which line is ahead, accumulated over $0\le x\le 3$. Which choice gives this quantity?
ap_calculus_ab-m28-r1.stimulus: {"kind":"graph","description":"Graph of two monthly profit-rate curves for a shop's product lines on 0 to 3 months. They cross at x=1 and x=2. Line P is above Line Q on 0<x<1 and 2<x<3, and below Line Q on 1<x<2.","data":{"x_axis":{"label":"time x (months)","min":0,"max":3,"tick_step":1},"y_axis":{"label":"profit rate (thousands of dollars per month)","min":0,"max":5,"tick_step":1},"curves":[{"name":"Line P","expression":"f(x)=x^2-2x+3","points":[[0,3],[1,2],[2,3],[3,6]]},{"name":"Line Q","expression":"g(x)=x+1","points":[[0,1],[1,2],[2,3],[3,4]]}],"intersections":[[1,2],[2,3]],"sign_of_f_minus_g":{"0<x<1":"positive","1<x<2":"negative","2<x<3":"positive"}}

options.why: Correct: the curves cross at x=1 and x=2, so split there and integrate top minus bottom on each piece: 5/6+1/6+5/6=11/6.
Integrates f-g over the whole interval without splitting at the crossings, so the region where Line Q is ahead cancels part of the other regions (signed area, not total gap).
Splits correctly but subtracts the last piece, wrongly treating the final region as negative even though Line P is above Line Q there.
Uses only the region between the two crossings and ignores the other two regions where the curves also enclose area on 0 to 3.

ap_calculus_ab-m28-r1.explanation_en: Setting f(x)=g(x) gives x^2-3x+2=(x-1)(x-2)=0, so the curves cross at x=1 and x=2, and the graph shows Line P above Line Q on 0<x<1 and 2<x<3 and below it on 1<x<2. Since the gap must be counted as positive everywhere, use top minus bottom on each piece. On [0,1], the integral of x^2-3x+2 is 5/6. On [1,2], the integral of g-f=-(x^2-3x+2) is 1/6. On [2,3], the integral of x^2-3x+2 is 5/6. The total is 11/6 thousand dollars. The single integral of f-g over [0,3] gives 3/2 because the negative signed contribution on [1,2] cancels part of the positive contributions, so it measures net difference, not total gap. The option that subtracts the last piece gives 1/6 because it treats a region where Line P is ahead as negative. The option using only [1,2] gives 1/6 but leaves out the two outer regions, which also lie between the curves.

ap_calculus_ab-m29-r0.stem: A field drainage channel has a base in the xy-plane (units in meters) that is the region bounded by $y=2\sqrt{x}$ and $y=x$, as shown. Cross sections of the channel perpendicular to the x-axis are rectangles whose height is one-half of the length of their base in the region. Which of the following is the volume of the channel, in cubic meters?

stimulus.description: Top view of a field drainage channel base in the first quadrant, bounded above by y = 2*sqrt(x) and below by y = x, for 0 <= x <= 4.

data.region: between the curves for 0<=x<=4; curves intersect at (0,0) and (4,4); 2*sqrt(x) is above x on (0,4)
data.cross_sections: perpendicular to the x-axis; rectangles whose base lies in the region and whose height is one-half of the base length

options.why: Correct: area = base times height = L*(L/2) = (1/2)L^2 with L = 2sqrt(x) - x, integrated over [0,4].
Uses the base squared but forgets the factor one-half in the height, so it is double the correct value.
Integrates (1/2)L, treating the rectangle area as a single length factor instead of base times height, so L is never squared.
Applies the one-half twice, using (1/4)L^2 as the area, because the factor is counted once in the height and again as if it also scaled the base.

ap_calculus_ab-m29-r0.explanation_en: On 0<x<4 the curve 2sqrt(x) lies above y=x, so the base length of a cross section is L = 2sqrt(x) - x. The height is L/2, so the rectangle's area is L*(L/2) = (1/2)(2sqrt(x) - x)^2. The volume is the integral from 0 to 4 of (1/2)(2sqrt(x) - x)^2 dx, which is about 3.733 cubic meters. The value 7.467 leaves out the one-half in the height, so it is twice the correct volume. The value 2.667 integrates (1/2)L, a single length factor, so it never squares the base length. The value 1.867 uses (1/4)L^2, counting the one-half twice.

ap_calculus_ab-m29-r1.stem: A company is pricing a custom storage bin. Its floor region in the $xy$-plane (feet) is bounded above by $y=4-0.25x^2$ and below by $y=0.5x^2-2$, between the points where the curves meet. Each cross section of the bin perpendicular to the $x$-axis is a rectangle whose base lies in the floor region and whose height is one-half of its base length. Which expression gives the volume of the bin in cubic feet, and what is its value?

stimulus.description: Table describing a storage bin whose floor region is bounded by two curves, with cross-section rule.

data.cross_sections: rectangles perpendicular to the x-axis, base in the floor region, height equal to one-half of the base length

options.why: Correct: base w=6-0.75x^2, height w/2, so area is w^2/2; integrate over the full intersection interval.
Treats the cross sections as squares (area w^2) and ignores that the height is only half the base.
Multiplies the base by the factor one-half but never multiplies by the base again for the height, so it gives half the floor area.
Uses an incorrect width (sum-like expression 2+0.25x^2 instead of upper minus lower), so the base length is wrong even though the area rule is right.

ap_calculus_ab-m29-r1.explanation_en: The curves meet where 4-0.25x^2 = 0.5x^2-2, so x^2=8 and x=±2.828. The base length of a cross section is upper minus lower, 6-0.75x^2. Its height is half the base, so its area is (1/2)(6-0.75x^2)^2. Integrating over the interval gives about 54.3 cubic feet. The integral without the one-half treats the rectangles as squares and doubles the volume. The integral with (1/2)(6-0.75x^2) only multiplies the base by one-half, so it gives half the floor area and omits the second factor of the base from the height. The integral using 2+0.25x^2 uses an incorrect base length, not the upper curve minus the lower curve.

ap_calculus_ab-m30-r0.stem: Water flows into a laboratory tank at rate $R(t)=4+3\sin(0.5t)$ liters per minute and drains out at rate $D(t)=2+0.1t$ liters per minute, for $0\le t\le 12$ minutes. The tank contains 30 liters at $t=0$. Which expression gives the volume of water, in liters, in the tank at $t=12$, and what is its approximate value?

stimulus.description: Inflow and outflow rate functions for a laboratory tank, with the initial volume and time interval.

options.why: Correct: final amount equals initial amount plus the integral of the net rate (inflow minus outflow).
Treats the net change as the final volume, forgetting the initial 30 liters.
Adds only the inflow to the initial volume, ignoring the water that drains out.
Treats the rates at t=12 as constant over the whole interval instead of integrating the varying rates.

ap_calculus_ab-m30-r0.explanation_en: The final volume equals the initial volume plus the net change, and the net change is the integral of inflow rate minus outflow rate. Here the net change is about 17.04 liters, so the volume is about 30 + 17.04 = 47.04 liters. The option giving only the integral of the net rate is wrong because it omits the 30 liters already in the tank, so it is a change in volume and not the volume. The option adding only the inflow integral to 30 is wrong because it ignores the water draining out and overstates the volume. The option multiplying the endpoint net rate by 12 is wrong because it treats the rates as constant, when both change over the interval, so the product is not the accumulated change.

ap_calculus_ab-f01-r0.title: Suspended Sediment Flow Past a Stream Gauge

stimulus.description: Table of sediment transport rate S(t), in kilograms per minute, measured at a stream gauge at five times during a 20-minute storm sampling period. Readings are unequally spaced.

data.title: Sediment transport rate at a stream gauge
data.function_info: S(t) is a continuous, differentiable function on 0<=t<=20 giving the rate at which sediment passes the gauge. S is increasing on [0,8] and decreasing on [8,20].

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Use a trapezoidal sum with the four subintervals determined by the table to approximate $\int_0^{20} S(t)\,dt$. Show the computation that leads to your answer, and interpret the value with units in context.

rubric_rows.criterion: Setup: uses the subinterval widths 3, 5, 6, 6 with the endpoint values from the table in trapezoid form
required_elements: (1/2)(width)(sum of endpoint values) for each subinterval

rubric_rows.criterion: Answer 84.5
Interpretation with units: total mass of sediment in kilograms passing the gauge over 0<=t<=20 minutes

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the left Riemann sum approximation of $\int_0^{20} S(t)\,dt$ using the same four subintervals. Then, using the fact that S is increasing on $[0,8]$, determine whether the left Riemann sum restricted to the subintervals within $[0,8]$ is an overestimate or an underestimate of $\int_0^8 S(t)\,dt$. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: Left sum = 3(2.0)+5(3.5)+6(6.0)+6(4.5) = 6+17.5+36+27 = 86.5. On [0,8] S is increasing, so on each subinterval the left endpoint value is the minimum of S there; the left sum 3(2.0)+5(3.5)=23.5 is an underestimate of the integral over [0,8].

rubric_rows.criterion: Setup: left endpoint values with correct widths
Answer 86.5
Underestimate on [0,8], justified by S increasing so left endpoint values are less than S on each subinterval
required_elements: left endpoint gives smaller value on each subinterval
common_errors: Applies the conclusion to all of [0,20] where S is not monotonic

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Using your trapezoidal approximation from part (a), find the approximate average rate of sediment transport over $0\le t\le 20$. Include units and state what this average represents.
parts.model_answer: Average value approx (1/20)(84.5) = 4.225 kilograms per minute. It is the constant rate that would carry the same total mass of sediment past the gauge in 20 minutes.

rubric_rows.criterion: Divides the part (a) approximation by 20
Units and meaning: kilograms per minute; constant rate giving the same total mass over the 20 minutes

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A student says the left Riemann sum from part (b) must be an underestimate of $\int_0^{20} S(t)\,dt$ because S is increasing on part of the interval. Is this reasoning justified? Explain using the behavior of S.
parts.model_answer: Not justified. S is increasing on [0,8] but decreasing on [8,20], so the left sum underestimates on the increasing part and overestimates on the decreasing part. The overall error direction cannot be concluded from monotonicity on only part of the interval.

rubric_rows.criterion: States the reasoning is not justified because S is increasing then decreasing, so left-sum errors have opposite directions on different parts
required_elements: S increasing on [0,8] but decreasing on [8,20]
alt_solutions: S is not monotonic on [0,20], so the left sum is not guaranteed to be an underestimate

ap_calculus_ab-f02-r1.title: Advertising Spend and Profit: Reading the Graph of f'

stimulus.description: Piecewise linear graph of f'(x), marginal profit in thousands of dollars per thousand dollars of advertising, for 0<=x<=8, through (0,4), (2,0), (4,-2), (6,0), (8,2).

x_axis.label: x (thousands of dollars spent on advertising)

y_axis.label: f'(x) (thousands of dollars of profit per thousand dollars of advertising)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A small business models its monthly profit, in thousands of dollars, as f(x), where x is thousands of dollars spent on advertising, 0<=x<=8. The function f is differentiable, and the graph of f' is shown; it is linear between the labeled points. Find all x in (0,8) at which f has a relative maximum or relative minimum. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: f'(x)=0 at x=2 and x=6. f' changes from positive to negative at x=2, so f has a relative maximum at x=2. f' changes from negative to positive at x=6, so f has a relative minimum at x=6.

rubric_rows.criterion: x=2 relative maximum with sign-change justification
required_elements: f' changes from positive to negative

rubric_rows.criterion: x=6 relative minimum with sign-change justification
required_elements: f' changes from negative to positive

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find all x-values in (0,8) at which the graph of f has a point of inflection. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: f'' is the slope of f'. The slope of f' is -2 on (0,2), -1 on (2,4), 1 on (4,6), and 1 on (6,8). f'' changes sign from negative to positive only at x=4, so the graph of f has a point of inflection at x=4 only. At x=2 and x=6, f'' does not change sign.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies x=4 as the only inflection point
common_errors: Including x=2 or x=6 because f' is zero or has a corner there

rubric_rows.criterion: Justifies using change of sign of f'' (f' changes from decreasing to increasing at x=4); f'' stays negative at x=2 and positive at x=6
required_elements: f'' changes from negative to positive at x=4
no sign change at x=2 and x=6

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the absolute maximum value of f on [0,8], given f(0)=10. Justify your answer using a candidates test and include units.
parts.model_answer: f is continuous on [0,8] because it is differentiable, so the Extreme Value Theorem applies. Candidates: x=0, 2, 6, 8. f(0)=10. f(2)=10+(1/2)(2)(4)=14. f(6)=14-(1/2)(2)(2)-(1/2)(2)(2)=10. f(8)=10+(1/2)(2)(2)=12. The absolute maximum is 14 thousand dollars at x=2.

rubric_rows.criterion: Names candidates (critical points and endpoints) and notes f is continuous on the closed interval
Computes f(2)=14 using area under f'
Compares with f(0)=10, f(6)=10, f(8)=12 and concludes the maximum is 14 thousand dollars

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A student claims: 'f'(6)=0 and f'(2)=0, so f has a relative extremum at both x=2 and x=6, and both must be maxima.' Is the reasoning correct? Explain.
parts.model_answer: Not correct. f'=0 only identifies candidates; the type of extremum depends on the sign change of f'. At x=2, f' goes positive to negative (maximum). At x=6, f' goes negative to positive (minimum), so x=6 is not a maximum.

rubric_rows.criterion: States f'=0 alone does not determine the type of extremum; sign change needed
Specific to graph: x=6 is a relative minimum since f' goes from negative to positive

ap_calculus_ab-f04-r0.title: Aquifer Layer Between Surface and Bedrock

stimulus.description: Field geologists model a vertical cross-section of a water-bearing sediment layer between an upper boundary f and a lower boundary g, with horizontal distance x and elevation y both in meters.

data.x_units: meters, horizontal distance from the survey stake
data.y_units: meters, elevation relative to a reference level
data.region: bounded by the two curves, between their two points of intersection

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinates of the two points where the curves f and g intersect. Then write an expression involving one integral for the cross-sectional area of the layer between the curves.
parts.model_answer: 9 - x^2 = x^2 - 1 gives x = -sqrt(5) and x = sqrt(5) (about -2.236 and 2.236). Area = integral from -sqrt(5) to sqrt(5) of [(9 - x^2) - (x^2 - 1)] dx = integral of (10 - 2x^2) dx.

rubric_rows.criterion: Intersection points
Integral with upper minus lower and correct limits
alt_solutions: 2 * integral from 0 to sqrt(5) of (10 - 2x^2) dx

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the cross-sectional area. Then find the volume of the layer if its cross-section is constant along a length of 12 meters. Include units.
parts.model_answer: Area = 40*sqrt(5)/3 ≈ 29.814 square meters. Volume = 12 * 29.814 ≈ 357.771 cubic meters.

rubric_rows.criterion: Area value
Volume value, area times length
Units
required_elements: square meters for area and cubic meters for volume

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The region is revolved about the horizontal line y = -3. Write an expression involving one integral for the volume of the resulting solid, and find its value.
parts.model_answer: Washers: outer radius f(x)+3 = 12 - x^2, inner radius g(x)+3 = x^2 + 2. V = pi * integral from -sqrt(5) to sqrt(5) of [(12 - x^2)^2 - (x^2 + 2)^2] dx = pi * integral of (140 - 28x^2) dx = 560*sqrt(5)*pi/3 ≈ 1311.2 cubic meters.

rubric_rows.criterion: Washer form with pi and difference of squared radii
Correct radii measured from y = -3
common_errors: Using f and g directly as radii

rubric_rows.criterion: Correct limits
Value with units
